answer: Separate-Hardware Beacon Attestation.** Each identity must emit a beacon signed by a physically unclonable circuit whose key never leaves the die. A sable coating of randomized dopant makes each chip's response unique and unforgeable. Verification nodes check that no two identities share a silicon fingerprint, so one operator can't mint extras from a single device. Acquiring N identities costs N fabricated chips plus the velvet cleanroom yield loss, a per-unit hardware bill no software sybil farm can amortize.
